fresh_leads.qualification_text: Requirements: Active and transferable U.S. government issued security clearance is required prior to start date.​ U.S. citizenship is required, as only U.S. citizens are eligible for a security clearance​ Security Clearance Type: DoD Clearance: Secret Security Clearance Status: Ability to obtain INTERIM U.S. government issued security clearance is required prior to start date Are you ready to explore the world of aerospace and defense? Do you want to learn from and collaborate with some of the greatest minds in the industry? At RTX, our internships, co-ops and full-time careers provide an exceptional foundation to work on complex problems, advance your skills and create a safer, more connected world. Discover opportunities to make a difference at RTX. What You Will Do The Systems Engineering and Test Capabilities (SE& TC) Center in Tucson, AZ is a multi-discipline organization responsible for designing, building and integrating state of the art missile and defense technology. On our team, you will work with reliability engineers to ensure that systems and products perform consistently and meet their expected lifetime requirements. You will analyze failure data, assess risks, and identify opportunities to improve performance. You will also collaborate with design, manufacturing, and test teams to integrate reliability into every stage of development. This position is an onsite role in Tucson, AZ You may support some of the following types of activities: Work on a reliability team to support systems design, integration, and/or test. Implement strategies to improve the reliability, availability, and maintainability of systems or equipment. Use data (failures, test results, field reports) to identify patterns and root causes of reliability issues. Performs reliability modeling and predictions using methods like Weibull analysis, FMEA, FMECAs, and fault tree analysis. Works closely with systems engineers, design engineers, manufacturing, and test teams to drive reliability into the product. Qualifications You Must Have Must be pursuing Bachelor's or Advanced degree in Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics (STEM) and actively enrolled through the completion of the internship/co-op session. Must have a minimum of 30 hours of credit by the start of the internship / co-op session. Academic, engineering club, or internship experience that includes reliability and root cause failure analysis Experience may be obtained through on-the-job experience, research, coursework, or projects. Qualifications We Prefer: Basic understanding of reliability concepts such as failure modes, MTBF, probability, and statistics. Experience with data analysis tools or languages (Excel, Python, MATLAB, or R). Familiarity with engineering problem‑solving methods like root cause analysis, FMEA, or fault tree logic. Strong attention to detail, analytical thinking, and willingness to learn complex systems. Good communication skills for presenting findings and collaborating with multidisciplinary teams. What We Offer Our values drive our actions, behaviors, and performance with a vision for a safer, more connected world. At RTX we value: Trust, Respect, Accountability, Collaboration, and Innovation. Systems & Silicon Validation: Post-silicon testing of physical chips and integrated systems to ensure they meet all functional, electrical, and performance specs. System Software: Development of foundational software, including firmware, drivers, and operating systems, that directly controls and interfaces with hardware. System Design: The process of defining, integrating, and mapping out hardware components such as PCBs, software modules, and interfaces into a complete product blueprint. System Architecture: Define the high-level structural framework, interfaces, and data-flow pathways between the CPU, memory, and peripherals. Packaging: A package is what is placed between the silicon and the board; and its design requires detailed electrical, electromagnetic, and mechanical simulations and analysis. This role is on-site, based out of Austin, TX or Santa Clara, CA. Who You Are Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in EE, Computer Engineering, Computer Science or Mechanical Engineering Coursework or projects in embedded systems, microwave and signal integrity, board-level design, or thermal/mechanical engineering using low-level programming (C/C++, Python) or hardware design and/or simulation tools (e.g., CAD, FEA, Verilog). Problem solver with strong foundational knowledge in one of these areas: electrical engineering, digital logic, computer architecture, or thermal/mechanical. Curious learner who is passionate about the intersection of software, silicon architecture, and the physical constraints of chip packaging and printed circuit boards (PCBs). What We Need Systems & Silicon Validation: Assist in post-silicon testing of physical microchips under real-world workloads to ensure they meet all functional, electrical, and performance specifications. System Software: Contribute to developing foundational software—including firmware, drivers, and operating systems—that directly controls and interfaces with the semiconductor hardware. System Design & Architecture: Help map out, define, and evaluate high-level structural frameworks, optimizing the power delivery and high-speed performance benchmarks of both the silicon components and the underlying PCBs. Semiconductor Packaging & Mechanical Design: Design and layout, Electromagnetic (signal integrity and power integrity), mechanical design, and stress analysis What You Will Learn Hands-on silicon experience using industry-standard lab equipment to bridge the gap between theoretical hardware design, physical packaging layouts, and real-world chips. Low-level software development by writing production-grade firmware, device drivers, and diagnostic tools that run directly on bare metal. Mechanical & thermal engineering for electronics by learning how structural stress, heat dissipation, thermal expansion, and mechanical shock affect the structural integrity and performance of PCBs and packages. Cross-functional collaboration working alongside world-class architects, mechanical designers, package engineers, and software teams to understand how complex, large-scale chip ecosystems are built from scratch. Knowledge of software development lifecycle (SDLC) Familiarity with working in an Agile/Scrum environment. Proven capabilities in creating verification documentation: Verification Plan and Reports, Traceability Matrix, and Standard Operating Procedures. Understanding of best practices for software development (such as Git, agile, code reviews, CI/CD). Experience working within a Quality Management System. Excellent communication skills (both written and oral) with the ability to communicate complicated ideas and information effectively at all levels.
